claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my child. I have one child - Alex, who's 16 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! Let me ask a few more questions about Alex to determine your eligibility.

Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training? If so, could you tell me what type of course or training they are undertaking?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Alex actually left school recently, but they've just registered with the local careers service to help figure out what they want to do next.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that detail. That's helpful to know.

Just to clarify, when Alex registered with the local careers service, was this an official registration for approved training or career guidance, or was it more of an informal arrangement to explore options?

Also, could you confirm whether Alex is currently:
- In any form of paid work (more than 24 hours per week)?
- Receiving any benefits in their own name (such as Universal Credit, Income Support, or Employment and Support Allowance)?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
It was an official registration with the careers service - they signed up properly to get guidance on their next steps.

And no, Alex isn't working at all at the moment, and they're not receiving any benefits in their own name either.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. This is very helpful!

Based on what you've told me, there's good news. Since Alex is 16 years old and has officially registered with a government-sponsored careers service, you may be able to continue receiving Child Benefit for Alex.

I just have a couple more questions to confirm eligibility:

1. Do you live in the UK?
2. Does Alex live with you?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK - we're in Manchester. And yes, Alex lives at home with me.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for confirming that. I now have all the information I need to assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great news! Based on the information you've provided, **you are eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

Here's a summary of why:

- **You qualify** because you live in the UK and are responsible for Alex, who lives with you.
- **Alex qualifies** because although they are 16 and have left school, the rules allow Child Benefit to continue for **20 weeks** when a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and officially registers with a government-sponsored careers service (which Alex has done).
- Alex meets all other conditions: they're not working 24+ hours per week, and they're not receiving benefits in their own name.

**Important to note:** This eligibility is for a 20-week period from when Alex registered with the careers service. During this time, if Alex starts approved education or training, enters paid work of 24+ hours per week, starts an apprenticeship in England, or begins receiving certain benefits in their own name, your eligibility may change.

I hope this helps! If you have any further questions about claiming Child Benefit, feel free to ask.

However, the rules state that Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17 year old leaves education or training and registers with a government-sponsored careers service. Alex has officially registered with the local careers service, which qualifies as a government-sponsored careers service. Additionally, Alex is not working (and certainly not 24+ hours per week), is not receiving any benefits in their own name (such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance), and has not started an apprenticeship in England. The claimant lives in the UK (Manchester), and Alex lives with them, meaning the claimant is responsible for Alex. All eligibility criteria are met for the 20-week extension period.
